comment: Known issues and limits of the emulator on the evaluated hosts, kept by hand. The results page (index.html) shows them under the support matrix, which it builds from evaluation/verification/. Not a result record. 'hosts' and 'modes' say where an issue applies ('all', or a list of host ids / emulator variants). 'kind' is one of: fails (a verification check fails because of it), limit (works, with a restriction), unverified (no host could check it), missing (not implemented). The task list (openspec/changes/staged-emulator-delivery/tasks.md) has the full account of each.

issues.title: No Vulkan on the ARM32 target
issues.detail: Vulkan is drawn by Mesa's CPU driver there, which crashes on 32-bit ARM. Video through Vulkan fails for the same reason.

issues.title: No Flutter on the ARM32 target
issues.detail: The Flutter SDK builds Linux applications for x86-64 and ARM64 only, so the ARM32 image has no Flutter application. Video through Flutter fails for the same reason.

issues.title: The display service is unstable on the ARM32 target, and ended once in a host-native VM on Linux
issues.detail: The Wayland compositor ends without a message now and then on the ARM32 target, on every host. The media and browser workloads start the display again and repeat; the graphics workload does not, so a graphics check can fail on one run and pass on the next. In one complete verification run on Linux the same happened in the host-native VM: five graphics checks failed, and all five passed when run again. The cause is not known.

issues.title: Host GPU graphics in container mode is verified nowhere
issues.detail: Linux: the host's GPU has NVIDIA's own driver, which the target's Mesa cannot draw with. macOS and Windows: the container engine's virtual machine has no GPU. A Linux host with an Intel or AMD GPU is needed to check this path.

issues.title: macOS: no host GPU graphics with the QEMU that setup installs
issues.detail: Homebrew's QEMU has no GPU-accelerated display device. An experimental QEMU build (./setup.sh --experimental-qemu) gives OpenGL ES on the host GPU in QEMU's own window; it is not part of the verified setup. Two of the source commits it builds from are on no branch any more (2026-11-16); setup.sh asks the servers for them by their ids, which works for as long as the servers keep them.

issues.title: Windows: host GPU graphics only in QEMU's own window, and not checked automatically
issues.detail: QEMU on Windows shows a display drawn on the host GPU nowhere but in its own window, which has no toolbar and takes no remote control keys, and offers no capture of it. It was checked by hand. QEMU also ends with an access violation after the target has shut down; the results are complete by then.

issues.title: Linux: a 4K display is cut off in the launcher's window in VM mode
issues.detail: QEMU 8.2 serves no more than 2560x2048 pixels to the window, so it shows the top left part of a 4K display, and the launcher says so. --option window=qemu shows all of it in QEMU's own window, without toolbar or remote control keys. QEMU 11 (macOS, Windows) serves all of it. Captures of a 4K display drawn on the host GPU are cut the same way; the checks compare that part and confirm the whole frame with emulated graphics.

issues.title: macOS: full screen needs the window to be the active application
issues.detail: A window started from a background session, and not made active by the system, reports full screen without growing; the check then says unavailable, and why. So it is while the Mac's screen is locked: on 2026-11-16 the four full screen checks were run that way and say unavailable, where they had passed on 2026-11-15.

issues.title: In VM mode the window gets part of a video's pictures, and shows a change on a quiet screen late
issues.detail: The window gets a VM's display from QEMU's display server, which sends a picture when the window has asked for one and its own clock comes round, and slows that clock down while the display does not change. Measured on macOS at 1080p in a host-native VM: 14 to 17 pictures a second of a 25 frames/s video (24.6 to 24.8 in container mode), and a change on a quiet screen after 0.12 s, or 0.5 to 0.7 s (0.2 to 0.9 s) once the screen had shown nothing new for 5 s or more (0.08 to 0.15 s in container mode). That QEMU's clock is the cause is read from how QEMU is built, not shown by a test. Not measured on Linux and Windows.

issues.title: Graphics results are lower while the display is shown in the launcher's window
issues.detail: Serving the display to the window costs the target's graphics some speed. On macOS at 1080p, with the window against the same image without it: plain Wayland drawing 25% lower in container mode and 37 to 38% on the simulated ARM targets; OpenGL ES 3 to 10% lower; Vulkan 9% lower in container mode, 12% in a host-native VM and 17% on the ARM64 target; the browser's drawing 13% lower in container mode and 18% in a host-native VM. Results for the evaluation are taken without a window. Not measured on Linux and Windows.

issues.title: The media workload stalls now and then in the ARM64 VM while its display is in the window
issues.detail: On macOS, in 3 of 10 runs of media-decode by the launcher with the window, a playback froze within seconds of a stream's start: the picture stayed, the sound to the host stopped, the target was idle, and the run had to be ended. The 3 runs without the window completed, as did the runs started from the STB simulator and every run in the other modes. The cause is not known. A video on demand title stalled in a like way once on Linux, also in the ARM64 VM.

issues.title: Flutter shows about a third of a video's frames
issues.detail: Of a 25 frames/s 720p stream, with emulated and with host graphics alike. The application gets decoded frames from a separate decoder and turns each into an image; one that shows video through a texture is not built.

issues.title: Sound from two target programs is not mixed
issues.detail: The target's audio device takes one player at a time.

issues.title: macOS: the sound checks do not record what left the output device
issues.detail: macOS has no private output device without installing an audio driver. The checks play at volume 0 and go by what the system's audio queue took and by the audio server's report of the player.

issues.title: The simulated ARM targets draw web pages far below real time
issues.detail: With the CPU emulated the test page renders at 0.05 to 3 frames/s, and most frames of an MSE stream do not reach the display on macOS and Windows. On Linux, where these targets draw through the host GPU, an ARM64 target loses few frames.

issues.title: TEXT has no key symbol in the target, and play shares one with play/pause
issues.detail: Both keys arrive with their own key codes. The image's browser is not an HbbTV browser, so what an HbbTV application would receive for each key is not settled.

issues.title: RedRat IR input
issues.detail: Not implemented; the launcher says so when it is asked for. No evaluation host has a RedRat device.

issues.title: P+, P-, TEXT and WEBTV do nothing in the simulator
issues.detail: The target's browser passes these four keys to a page as keys without a name, so the user interface cannot tell them apart. The channel is changed with Up and Down and with the digits.

issues.title: The films of the video on demand application need the internet, and servers that are not this project's
issues.detail: Big Buck Bunny, Elephants Dream, Sintel and Tears of Steel are MPEG-DASH streams served by Akamai, BBC R&D and the Shaka Player project. A title the target cannot reach is refused with a message; a stream that moves has to be replaced in titles.json. The test title on the device plays without a network.

issues.title: A video on demand title stalled once on the ARM64 target
issues.detail: In the first of two runs on Linux the test title stopped right after it started and reported nothing more; the user interface took keys again afterwards, and the second run passed. Not seen in the other modes. The cause is not known.

issues.title: Windows: video on demand fails in the ARM VMs when the player changes representation
issues.detail: In two runs out of two each, the test title failed where the player leaves its smallest representation (426x240). ARM64: the browser's renderer process ends with 'video meta uses 432x240 instead of 426x240' from the GStreamer libav plugin; the simulator starts the browser again. ARM32: the title was refused once ('Unable to allocate memory'), and once the picture stayed at the smallest size while the player reported 1280x720. The title that stays at one representation played each time; the films were not reached. Container mode and the host-native VM pass. The cause is not known. On 2026-11-17, after the installation had been removed and made anew and the ARM64 image built again from the same definition (0.6.0), the ARM64 check passed in three runs out of three; what made the difference is not known. The ARM32 check failed in its one run that day, in the title that stays at one representation, the renderer process ending with the message quoted for ARM64.

issues.title: On a simulated ARM target the simulator shows what a key did after about a second, and a channel at about one picture a second
issues.detail: Timed on macOS at 1080p from the launcher's window (evaluation/stb-timings): the user interface answers a key within 0.05 s, but the changed picture reaches the window after 0.9 s on the ARM64 target and 1.2 s on ARM32 (0.08 s in container mode, 0.12 s in a host-native VM). A channel change shows after 2.3 s and 3.0 s (0.16 s and 0.28 s), and of a channel's 25 pictures a second 1.4 to 1.5 and 0.7 to 0.9 reach the window. The home screen is there 11.8 s and 29.7 s after the launch (0.9 s and 1.3 s). Not timed on Linux and Windows.

issues.title: The resource benchmark reads lower when it is started from the simulator on a simulated ARM target
issues.detail: bench does not take the display, so the simulator's browser stays up and keeps drawing beside it. On macOS, 9 of its 13 results on the ARM64 target and 10 on ARM32 were 11 to 35% lower than when the launcher ran it; in container mode and in a host-native VM its processor and memory tests agreed within 7%. The workloads that take the display report from the simulator what they report from the launcher with the same window. Results for the evaluation are recorded by running the workloads themselves.

issues.title: A performance workload that uses the display cannot be ended from the simulator
issues.detail: The graphics, media and web workloads take over the display, and the user interface is stopped until they are done; no key ends them early. The channels are the five-second reference streams, played in a loop.

issues.title: Full matrix run, comparison report, and disk space and time measurements
issues.detail: The complete host matrix has not been run and the Slidev comparison is not written. Of the disk space and time values in evaluation/footprint.md the macOS host's are measured, and the Windows host's but for three: the build times of the host-native and the ARM64 VM image from an empty engine, and of all four targets in one engine, for which its disk had too little free space (27 to 34 GB). The Linux host has its performance evaluation times and one size.

issues.title: Hosts of the matrix that have not been run
issues.detail: macOS on x86-64, and Ubuntu 22.04 and 26.04 (the Linux host is Kubuntu 24.04). The setup script's dnf, zypper and pacman paths were run in containers only.
